newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Declarations, decisions of OAU summit in Zimbabwe.
newsitem.headline: Declarations, decisions of OAU summit in Zimbabwe.

text.p: The Organisation of African Unity (OAU) ended a three-day summit in Zimbabwe on Wednesday. The following are highlights of its declarations and decisions:
-- unanimously agreed and unreservedly condemned the coup in Sierra Leone as an enormous setback for democracy in Africa and called for urgent restoration of constitutional order.
-- urged Africa and the international community to assist Laurent Kabila's government in the Democratic Republic of Congo in its programme to reconstruct the central African country.
-- noted encouraging signs in the peace processes in Liberia, Somalia and Angola and progress towards negotiations in Burundi.
-- reiterated general support for the Palestine Liberation Organisation and its current efforts to resume stalled peace talks with Israel.
-- elected three commissioners, from Tunisia, South Africa and Egypt, to the African Commission for Human and People's Rights.

-- renewed call for lifting of sanctions against Libya and call to U.N. Security Council to accept one of three options -- trial in a third country chosen by council, trial by Scottish judges at International Court of Justice in the Hague or special criminal tribunal in Hague -- to resolve case of two Libyans suspected of involvement in Lockerbie bombing in 1988.
-- re-elected to an unprecedented third four-year term Salim Ahmed Salim of Tanzania as Secretary-General of the OAU.
-- expressed need for a united African stand on issues of trade, debt and general development.

-- agreed on the need for all African countries, helped by foreign governments, the World Health Organisation (WHO), the World Bank and other multilateral organisations, to fight resurgent malaria which is killing millions of people.
-- agreed to hold next annual ordinary OAU summit in the West African state of Burkina Faso.
